pohick-church-lorton.assessment: Pohick Church is one of the oldest and most historically significant churches in Northern Virginia — originally built in 1774 and known as the parish of George Washington, George Mason, and other Virginia Founders. It is a landmark of American religious history. However, it remains affiliated with the Episcopal Church (TEC), which has undergone systematic theological abandonment since the 1970s — ordaining women as priests and bishops, affirming same-sex marriage, and ordaining LGBTQ+ clergy. The historic beauty of this church and its colonial American legacy are genuinely compelling, but the TEC institutional framework is doctrinally unreliable. Men seeking sound biblical preaching and complementarian theology should consider ACNA alternatives in Northern Virginia (such as The Falls Church Anglican or Truro Anglican), which left TEC precisely over these issues. Visit Pohick as a history lesson; find a sound church for your soul.

score_notes.scripture: TEC rejects inerrancy; Scripture alongside tradition, reason, experience.
score_notes.gender: Episcopal Church ordains women to all orders and is officially LGBTQ-affirming (blessing of same-sex marriages). Black per rubric.
score_notes.cultural: TEC officially affirming since 2015 GC marriage-rite vote; Diocese of Virginia is progressive.

score_notes.preaching: Holy Eucharist Rite I and Rite II services — BCP liturgical.

portico-church-charlottesville.assessment: Portico Church is a Gospel-centered Southern Baptist congregation near downtown Charlottesville, pastored by Rev. Jason Conner under the BGAV (Baptist General Association of Virginia). The BGAV affiliation warrants mild caution — it is a state-level convention that can trend more moderate than the national SBC on cultural and gender issues. The church's own branding is 'Gospel Centered,' which is encouraging, and the Baptist Faith & Message 2000 provides a solid baseline for doctrine. Before committing, a man would want to attend in person, review sermon content, and ask directly about women in leadership and the church's stance on cultural issues. The orthodox foundation is likely solid; the BGAV context is the variable.

potters-house-dallas.assessment: The Potter's House is T.D. Jakes' mega-church in Dallas. Jakes came from a Oneness Pentecostal (modalist) background — he has made statements toward Trinitarianism in recent years but has never clearly repudiated his Oneness roots. His theology is prosperity-adjacent, his preaching is motivational rather than expository, and the church operates as a personality-driven ministry with limited accountability. The Oneness background alone is a serious concern for anyone committed to Nicene orthodoxy.
